question: Is oral sex permissible between a husband and wife?
answer:
Now again, the issue of oral intercourse... And again, if you are watching only this one video, I've given another video about what is forbidden in intimacy, so you can watch that video as well, and then watch this in conjunction with that one.

Oral intercourse does come under the gray area that the Shari'ah is not explicit about between the husband and wife. And we actually do not have a lot of quotations about oral intercourse. The reason being that oral intercourse, generally speaking, was a sexual habit that was frowned upon in most Eastern cultures. It is something that is not embraced; it is more of a Western notion.

And this is actually historically true; I'm not just inventing this. Even the ancient Indian book of the Kama Sutra, if you actually look it up, actually mentions this act as not being between husband and wife; really, it's mentioned amongst other segments of sexuality. And the pre-Islamic Arabs actually also knew of this act, and they considered it to be vulgar and crude, not something that is done by noble people.

And this is indicated by the famous incident in the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, when one of the negotiators basically insulted the Sahabah by saying that they're going to abandon the Prophet. Abu Bakr as-Siddiq became so angry (that shy, that modest, that humble, that pure person), he became so angry and enraged that he lost his temper and he uttered a profanity. And this is so atypical of Abu Bakr as-Siddiq. But in his love for the Prophet ﷺ, when that man came and dared suggest that Abu Bakr is going to abandon the Prophet ﷺ, and the Sahabah are going to abandon the Prophet ﷺ, his emotions went from zero to 1,000 in one second, and he wanted to utter the worst vulgarity that they could ever utter, to get his point across to this man.

And he said something that translates as (and again, it is explicit; this video is not meant except for an adult audience)... He literally said, "Go suck on the clitoris of al-Lat." This is literally what Abu Bakr as-Siddiq said: "Umsus bazr al-Lat." Al-Lat was their female goddess.

Now, this is a very interesting curse. It actually demonstrates that oral intercourse was known to them, and it was an insult, and it was the highest insult, and it was an insult for a man to do this, because they considered it to be demeaning and vulgar. So it's very clear that Eastern cultures generally, and yes, Arab cultures, even pre-Islam and throughout most of Islamic history, they viewed this act as not being noble.

But as I explained in my other video about what is haram in sexual actions and whatnot, nobility does not translate into haram and halal. Something can be ignoble, and it doesn't make it haram. Something can be against the purity of the fitrah, and it doesn't make it haram; you can say it is makruh. And therefore haram and halal is not based primarily upon nobility. It is based upon what Allah and His Messenger have said.

And therefore, because of this, I understand that... By the way, you're not going to find classical discussions in the books of fiqh about oral intercourse. You will find about masturbation, you will find about anal, you will find about so many other things that were known, but you will not find a detailed discussion about oral intercourse, because it was not something that was common at all.

Now, you will find very, very few references to it. And of those references is that some scholars did allow it. The famous Hanbali scholar al-Qadi Abu Ya'la, he said that a man may kiss the vagina of his wife before intercourse without karahah, and after intercourse it is makruh. And he said the same applies for a woman: that she may kiss the man's organ with passion. He actually said this: that with passion, she may enjoy the man's organ. And he also said this is the position of 'Ata', the tabi'i.

And in the famous al-Fatawa al-Hindiyyah of Hanafi fiqh, the famous Fatawa Hindiyyah that was compiled, I believe, under the Alamgir timeframe (not 100% sure, sorry, don't quote me on that)... By the way, Fatawa Hindiyyah is not that old; it's only like 200, 300 years old. So it's not one of the ancient books, but it is a relatively more modern one. In the Fatawa al-Hindiyyah, it says that if a man inserts his penis into his wife's mouth, some have said this is makruh, and some have said that it is not makruh. So we have that reference there.

And al-Qurtubi, the famous Andalusian scholar, he mentions in his tafsir that Asbagh al-Maliki, the famous earlier Maliki scholar, one of the classical scholars of the Maliki madhhab, says that it is allowed for the man (this is explicit, brothers and sisters), it is allowed for the man to lick his wife's organ. "Yalhasuhu bil-lisan": it literally says to lick. So we have some very few references that some of our scholars considered it to be permissible.

At the same time, a lot of modern scholars considered it to be impermissible, and I can quote you like five or ten. And this is generally modern fatawa; as I said, in earlier books it's not really discussed. And they bring a number of evidences for this.

So the first evidence that they bring that it is impermissible is the whole genre of verses that I already quoted, and a hadith: approach women, they are your cultivation; approach them from their harth, from their field. And they say that the mouth is not an orifice of cultivation. So Allah 'azza wa jall is saying approach them as if they're fields, as if they're cultivation. Now, this is a very weak evidence, because by unanimous consensus it is allowed for a man and a woman to play together with each other's hands until ejaculation is achieved. And a man may ejaculate onto the body of his wife, and nobody will say it is haram, and he will do it intentionally. It does not contradict the verse. So it's a very weak way to refute this.

Another thing that those who make it haram say: they say that the mouth is a noble organ, and the mouth does dhikr, and the mouth recites the Qur'an, and so we should not put our private parts in it. And to respond to this, one can say that that might be a valid point, that it is a noble organ, but it doesn't make it sinful; it doesn't make it haram. You can say that it is discouraged, you can say that it's not befitting, but to say it is haram is to bring Allah's sin, and maybe Allah's wrath or Allah's curse (or not necessarily wrath and curse), but you're saying that it is potentially punishable.

And the evidence, or the notion, that the mouth is noble and dhikr is done: well, okay, ghibah and namimah is a worse sin than kissing the organ of your spouse, for example, and it is done by the mouth. So what are you going to do? If somebody does ghibah, we tell him, "You don't read the Qur'an"? If somebody slanders, does buhtan, we're going to tell him, "Don't do dhikr of Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala"? So the two are separate things, and you cannot bring the notion of tahrim just because you said that the mouth is a noble organ. The max that can be said is that it is not a noble act. I can understand this, but as I said, to say something is not noble does not make it sinful in the eyes of Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala.

Now, I think one of the strongest ways to actually say that it is makruh, or maybe more than makruh, is to bring up the issue of najasah, and to say that potentially najasah is going to be put into one's mouth. And to respond to this, one could say that the majority of the madhhabs, actually three of the madhhabs, say that semen is not najas. So three of the madhhabs actually say that it is not najas. And then one can also respond that, by unanimous consensus, a small amount of najasah is overlooked, because you cannot protect yourself. Now, what constitutes small, that is going to be another controversy.

And still, I would say that this argument of najasah... As we said, it is best to avoid najasah, but in and of itself, touching something najis or of that nature, it's not something that is going to incur Allah's sin. And if it is done for a reason, it is permissible by unanimous consensus, as I explained in the previous question: a person changes the diaper of their child, and that might be najis, or you cleanse yourself, and that is najis. So you wash it off afterwards. And it might not be noble; it might not be something that is dignified. But something that is undignified does not necessarily become sinful in the eyes of Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala.

And therefore, what I would conclude is that oral intimacy is something that one cannot say is sinful in the eyes of Allah. But at the same time, one should understand, frankly, that this is a habit that we are picking up because of the prevalence of it in the cultures that we live in. Not that there's anything wrong with every single habit, but this particular habit, it was not something that was common or the norm in the majority of cultures, and especially in Muslim lands and cultures. And that is why one does not find a discussion of this in the classical books; you find just a quick reference here and there. And generally speaking, we do find permissibility in some of the previous 'ulama.

And I want to quote you a fatwa from one of the scholars who gave this with regards to oral intercourse. He said, "In conclusion, it has now become clear that oral intercourse is not prohibited, but it is not the normal choice for committed Muslims and Muslimas. Despite the fact that oral sex is not haram, it is completely disgusting and does not conform to the pure taste and the decency of a Muslim's personality." I am sympathetic to this. So it is not haram; you're not going to be sinful. But at the same time, let's try to cultivate haya and try to do that which is the best.

Another fatwa, from a modern Hanafi shaykh, Mufti Ibrahim Desai. He writes that it is makruh, "because the mouth is not an orifice of najis, and because the mouth is used for reciting the Qur'an and for doing dhikr," end quote. So, makruh. I agree with this fatwa: that oral intercourse is not haram, but it should be makruh.

And if the couple feels that they must engage in this, they really should make sure that najasah is avoided and nothing of that nature is ingested. Of course, the madhi, or the pre-seminal fluid, is najas, so keep that point in mind. And if it is done, then it should not be something that... And again, I mean, the problem comes, dear brothers and sisters, that people have been raised in a society where certain acts have been absorbed by them. They want to do these things. And if they are told that it is not allowed within a marriage, it might actually cause problems for many of them. Sometimes people convert to Islam, and they are totally accustomed to a certain lifestyle. So we cannot give a blanket fatwa to every single couple.

The default, as I have said, and this is the position I'm advocating, is that **it is not haram, it is not sinful, but I'm not giving the green light. It is makruh.** And one should strive to one's best to attain a more noble or more purified level. But if one does it, one will not be punished by Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala. And by the way, interestingly, just interestingly, Jewish rabbis as well, many of them, they also forbid this; I'm talking about the Orthodox strand.

And also, before I conclude this question, I want to again be very clear here that this is something that is above and beyond normal intercourse. So if a woman feels that she does not want to engage in this, the husband cannot force her. Because she is required by Islamic law to be accessible for regular intercourse, if there are no other impediments; she is required by our Shari'ah to allow him to have intercourse with her. She is not required by our Shari'ah to satisfy every fetish or every desire of his that is beyond that which is mainstream and normal. And so if she finds this issue problematic, she should speak with him, and she should not be forced.

That having been said, the flip side as well: if the husband... it might cause problems as well. So they should try to find some type of middle ground or whatnot in this regard, because, again, we want couples to find marital happiness within themselves; we want them to find sexual happiness within marriage and from each other. And so these things need to be discussed within the marriage, and couples need to negotiate what can and cannot be done within the confines of their bedroom. But from a purely technical perspective, she should not be forced to do something that is above and beyond what is regular intercourse. And the two can negotiate what can be done, and Allah 'azza wa jall knows best.
